title: A settings file
description:
Write functions that save and load a simple settings file of `key=value` lines:

```lua-norun
save_settings(path, settings)   -- writes one "key=value" line per entry, sorted by key, and returns true
load_settings(path)             -- reads the file back into a table, or returns nil and an error message when
                                -- the file cannot be opened
append_line(path, text)         -- adds text and a newline at the end of the file, creating it if needed
count_lines(path)               -- the number of lines in the file
```

When loading:
- spaces around the key and value are ignored, and blank lines and lines starting with `#` are skipped;
- a value that is a number becomes a number, `true` and `false` become booleans, anything else stays text;
- a line without `=` is skipped.

```
# game settings
volume = 11
fullscreen=true
name = Ada Lovelace
```

loads as `{ volume = 11, fullscreen = true, name = "Ada Lovelace" }`.

solution.solution.lua:
function save_settings(path, settings)
    local keys = {}
    for k in pairs(settings) do keys[#keys + 1] = k end
    table.sort(keys)
    local f <close> = assert(io.open(path, "w"))
    for _, k in ipairs(keys) do
        f:write(k, "=", tostring(settings[k]), "\n")
    end
    return true
end

local function convert(value)
    if value == "true" then return true end
    if value == "false" then return false end
    return tonumber(value) or value
end

function load_settings(path)
    local f, err = io.open(path, "r")
    if not f then return nil, err end
    local settings = {}
    for line in f:lines() do
        if not line:match("^%s*$") and not line:match("^%s*#") then
            local key, value = line:match("^%s*(.-)%s*=%s*(.-)%s*$")
            if key and key ~= "" then settings[key] = convert(value) end
        end
    end
    f:close()
    return settings
end

function append_line(path, text)
    local f <close> = assert(io.open(path, "a"))
    f:write(text, "\n")
end

function count_lines(path)
    local n = 0
    for _ in io.lines(path) do n = n + 1 end
    return n
end

hints: `io.open(path, "w")` empties the file first; `"a"` adds to the end. A `local f <close>` variable is closed when the function ends.
`line:match("^%s*(.-)%s*=%s*(.-)%s*$")` splits a line at its first `=` and trims both parts.
unitTests:
local function write_file(path, text)
    local f = assert(io.open(path, "w"))
    f:write(text)
    f:close()
end

local function read_file(path)
    local f = assert(io.open(path, "r"))
    local text = f:read("a")
    f:close()
    return text
end

test("saving writes sorted lines", function()
    check_eq(save_settings("out.cfg", { volume = 11, name = "Ada", fullscreen = true }), true)
    check_eq(read_file("out.cfg"), "fullscreen=true\nname=Ada\nvolume=11\n")
end)

test("loading converts values", function()
    write_file("in.cfg", "# game settings\nvolume = 11\nfullscreen=true\n\n  name = Ada Lovelace  \nratio=0.75\nmuted = false\nbroken line\n")
    check_eq(load_settings("in.cfg"), { volume = 11, fullscreen = true, name = "Ada Lovelace", ratio = 0.75, muted = false })
end)

test("save and load round trip", function()
    local settings = { width = 1280, height = 720, title = "My Game", vsync = false }
    save_settings("round.cfg", settings)
    check_eq(load_settings("round.cfg"), settings)
end)

test("a missing file", function()
    local result, err = load_settings("no-such-file.cfg")
    check_eq(result, nil)
    check(type(err) == "string" and err:find("no%-such%-file") ~= nil, "the error names the file")
end)

test("appending and counting lines", function()
    write_file("log.txt", "")
    append_line("log.txt", "started")
    append_line("log.txt", "loaded level 1")
    append_line("new-log.txt", "created")
    check_eq(read_file("log.txt"), "started\nloaded level 1\n")
    check_eq(count_lines("log.txt"), 2)
    check_eq(count_lines("new-log.txt"), 1)
end)
